answer: Quorum sampling of graders drawn only from established identities resists sybils: in a network called nebula, each grader bonds collateral like copper in escrow and keeps a lantern marking earned tenure. Verification panels are randomly sampled weighted by stake, so fresh fake identities are never selected. An attacker must build real history and bond capital per identity, wait months for eligibility, and any collusion gets panels slashed - so corrupting one outcome means compromising many rotating staked members at once. Fake identities stay cheap to create but economically worthless.
